{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABcqLLcw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGMUYg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 132, "title": "Configure the bundled PC-9821Ap FreeDOS(98) desktop for high-memory DOS and measure usable conventional memory", "body": "## Problem

A user successfully booted FreeDOS(98), installed a PC-98 DOS game to the IDE HDD, and on launching the game saw a Japanese warning that it **requires approximately 540 KiB of conventional memory**. The minimal FreeDOS installation does not include the `MEM` utility or a high-memory/XMS manager. In particular, the newly released **default PC-9821Ap DOS browser desktop**, built by [Issue #130 / PR #131](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/130), currently contains:

```ini
DOS=LOW
SHELL=A:\COMMAND.COM A:\ /P /E:256
```

Its builder [`tools/prepare_desktop.py`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tools/prepare_desktop.py) installs only the pinned GPL kernel/FreeCOM, PROBE, notices and original configuration; **no XMS manager or memory-inspection utility is included**. The browser now starts with this 128 MiB FAT16 FreeDOS IDE HDD automatically, which makes its boot configuration the natural place to address this usability problem.

The PC-9821Ap profile advertises **640 KiB conventional + 3 MiB extended RAM**, but guest RAM installed above 1 MiB **does not itself increase the largest allocatable DOS conventional-memory block**. A working PC-98 XMS manager, HMA access, DOS's high loading and minimizing resident driver/shell allocations may help. **A line change to `DOS=HIGH` alone, without a working manager, is not a fix.**

This Issue targets the **default bundled FreeDOS(98) desktop on Ap**, not an arbitrary user's uploaded/previously exported HDI and not Windows or general numerical-FPU/DPMI support. Existing small, hash-pinned `DOS=LOW` research fixtures should not be silently rewritten merely to change the default desktop.

## Expected outcome

**A fresh public-browser visit** automatically boots the bundled FreeDOS(98) desktop on PC-9821Ap **with an appropriately licensed PC-98 XMS/HMA memory manager loaded and a verified working `DOS=HIGH` configuration**, allowing DOS games to access significantly more conventional memory without users manually editing `FDCONFIG.SYS` or locating driver binaries.

The concrete compatibility goal is to make **at least 540 KiB (552,960 bytes) available in the largest conventional DOS allocation** after the real DOS shell is ready, where achievable with the project's PC-9821Ap 640 KiB base-memory configuration. Do **not** claim this threshold based on total free RAM, 3 MiB of XMS, an allocator counter outside the guest, or the presence of the configuration text alone: measure the guest's **largest successful/requestable contiguous DOS memory block**. If testing proves that the pinned FreeDOS(98) variant or the emulated memory/CPU/BIOS lacks a necessary feature, identify the **specific, reproducible blocker**, implement a bounded original-Rust correction with independent regression coverage as appropriate, or open a linked, actionable `task` for a substantial separate subsystem. **Do not silently fall back to `DOS=LOW` and report completion.**

A memory-manager utility such as a PC-98-compatible `MEM.EXE` is useful for transparent guest inspection, but may be omitted from the default disk if its license/integration or runtime cost is not justified; the **independent guest allocator measurement is mandatory regardless of whether `MEM` ships**.

## Known public sources and licensing considerations

Candidate PC-98-native source, **not yet integrated or proven working on this emulator**:

- [HimemX(98) author/maintainer repository](https://github.com/lpproj/himemx.nec), [release `v3.34-nec98-20160913`](https://github.com/lpproj/himemx.nec/releases/tag/v3.34-nec98-20160913), distributed archive [`himemx334_nec98_20160913.zip`](https://github.com/lpproj/himemx.nec/releases/download/v3.34-nec98-20160913/himemx334_nec98_20160913.zip). Its [HimemX98.txt](https://github.com/lpproj/himemx.nec/blob/master/HimemX98.txt) explicitly describes DOS use on PC-9801/9821 with **386+ CPU and extended memory** and `DEVICE=HIMEMX.EXE`. The public source repository carries **`LICENSE.txt` with the Artistic License**: check the exact release archive's notices, source relationship and executable redistribution conditions before bundling.
- [FreeDOS kernel documentation for `DOS=HIGH`](https://help.fdos.org/en/hhstndrd/cnfigsys/dos.htm): load an applicable XMS manager *first*. Test the pinned PC-98 kernel's exact behavior; do not assume IBM-PC behavior.
- Optional [PC-98 MEM release](https://github.com/lpproj/mem.nec/releases/tag/mem1.11p1-20181113) for a real memory report. Verify the exact binary/license before considering publication. This is **not a reason to block** building a small, original MIT guest diagnostic.
- If the HMA alone is insufficient, investigate an appropriately licensed [PC-98 EMM386](https://github.com/lpproj/emm386.nec) and UMB/DEVICEHIGH only when evidence warrants it. EMM386 introduces additional CPU/paging/driver compatibility risk; do **not** unconditionally add it, silently assume EMS exists, or broaden this Issue into Windows/DPMI support.

All these tools are **guest DOS software**, not emulator implementations. No existing emulator code, commercial games, proprietary BIOS/ROM/font dumps or private media may be copied into this repository.

## Context and implementation points

- [`tools/prepare_desktop.py`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tools/prepare_desktop.py): generates a deterministic **128 MiB FAT16** logical disk from checksum-pinned FreeDOS and original MIT code, with a **655,360-byte sparse nonzero prefix**; writes `FDCONFIG.SYS`, builds [`fixtures/desktop-manifest.json`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/fixtures/desktop-manifest.json), source archive and published `web/freedos/` assets. Adding a resident driver changes file allocation, hashes and possibly the prefix length. Keep the sparse/chunked transfer rather than publishing a full 128 MiB file.
- [`src/firmware.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/firmware.rs): initializes RAM/BWA fields, PC-98 BIOS synthetic services, and A20/HMA-related interfaces. [`src/bus.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/bus.rs) allocates 4 MiB for Ap, including 640 KiB conventional; verify guest-addressable HMA, actual XMS driver detection, A20 management and conventional-memory behavior against the PC-98 hardware interface without hacks for the game's filename.
- [`docs/desktop-validation.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/desktop-validation.md) and [`tests/browser/desktop.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tests/browser/desktop.spec.js): real release-Wasm cold/reset checks, authentic FreeDOS prompt `A:\>`, interactive PROBE/ECHO, FDD hot-insert, boot selection, restore/export, startup speed, memory, hash and source publication.
- [`docs/licenses.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/licenses.md): the bundled DOS is **publicly redistributed**, unlike the private test-only FreeDOS floppy/HDD fixtures. Any added XMS manager or optional MEM utility requires its **own reviewed rights, exact binary/source provenance, checksums and legally sufficient notices/source distribution**; update [`web/licenses.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/licenses.html), the publication manifest, the source tar and the strict approved-assets audit as necessary. Publishing the compiled binary alone on Pages is not sufficient evidence of compliance.
- The previous [Issue #126 FDD2 hot insertion](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/126) and [Issue #127 large HDI support](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/127) must not regress. This work **does not** require a copyrighted game or manually uploaded boot floppy.

## Implementation and investigation

1. **Measure baseline first.** On the current published desktop with `DOS=LOW`, use an **original MIT guest DOS program** (for instance, an INT 21h/AH=48h allocation query using the DOS-defined largest-available-block failure return, with guard and restoration checks) to determine the largest **allocatable contiguous conventional memory block**, in paragraphs and bytes, after FreeCOM is resident. Keep the measurement reproducible in native and production-Wasm tests. Do not confuse request failure BX or total free XMS with actually available DOS memory. Check that the measurement method itself does not retain or leak conventional allocations.
2. **Select and pin one suitable PC-98 driver.** Inspect release binary/archive and matching source/Artistic or other notices; verify distribution rights. Add a **reproducible, checksum-locked fetch/extract** with a bounded download and exact archive member. Preserve the complete corresponding source/notices according to the applicable license. Do not depend on an unpinned latest download or source code from an emulator.
3. **Build the Ap desktop with the manager before `DOS=HIGH`.** Use the correct PC-98-supported `DEVICE=...` path and `DOS=HIGH` syntax for this pinned FreeDOS version, retaining its real boot path, FreeCOM, FAT16 geometry, boot selection, sparse prefix and existing user-visible startup. Do not force an XMS driver into the PC-9801VM V30-only boot path; leave the historical `minimal.hdm`/low-DOS fixture hashes intact unless a separately justified fixture is added.
4. **Observe real operation.** Verify the driver actually initializes through real guest instructions, DOS genuinely relocates appropriate resident code/data to HMA and XMS/A20/BIOS interactions behave coherently; observe actual runtime state, not just output text. Retest keyboard, IRQ, BIOS disk access, HDD guest writes/exports, mount/reset/profile switch and 128 MiB desktop startup.
5. **Measure and iterate.** Compare conventional largest-allocation before and after on the same Ap RAM profile. Aim for **>= 540 KiB contiguous** at a clean DOS prompt; if still below, quantify what remains resident, consider only justified settings/driver refinements and fix evidenced emulator incompatibilities with independent CPU/memory tests. Explain any practical memory ceiling or incompatibility; do not claim the user-reported game now runs unless that game has actually been tested.
6. **Keep publication correct.** Revise desktop manifest checksums, source/notice archives, publication allowlist/audit and README/license guidance. Verify sparse startup, deterministic regeneration and explicit export/reimport. Ensure no private disk/game data and no proprietary BIOS/font assets enter Pages.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh Ap desktop and **Restore FreeDOS HDD** both install the same validated PC-98 XMS manager and use an actually functioning **`DOS=HIGH`** configuration; cold/reset reach a responsive actual FreeDOS/FreeCOM shell and can execute the original PROBE/ECHO guest commands. No host-invented DOS prompt. The configuration must not silently regress to `DOS=LOW`.
- [ ] Report the **baseline and final largest contiguous conventional DOS allocation** in paragraphs and bytes, measured with original real guest code on identical Ap configuration, cold/reset. Assert both **a genuine improvement and the 540 KiB target if achievable**. If a proven architectural boundary prevents 540 KiB, record the independently reproduced blocker, test the maximum demonstrated improvement, and keep remaining compatibility work in an actionable linked `task` rather than claiming the user's game is fixed.
- [ ] Prove that the selected PC-98 memory manager initializes and the relevant HMA/XMS/A20 functionality is operational, including representative memory protection/invalid access and recovery behavior. Add original independently reproducible failing-before/passing-after tests for any emulator CPU/BIOS/memory corrections; do not bypass PC-98 hardware semantics or hardcode a particular game.
- [ ] Pin driver exact **release URL, binary bytes/hash, source relationship, license notices and redistribution basis**, rebuild the audited deterministic FAT16 desktop, update publication manifests and accompany any new publicly served binary with source and notices as its actual license requires. Update the legal attribution and same-site source links. Preserve the 128 MiB sparse template architecture and measured startup network size/memory rather than adding a raw HDI to Pages.
- [ ] Preserve PC-9801VM legacy behavior, original V30 guest fixtures and pinned `DOS=LOW` controls; preserve Ap floppy hot insert, IDE large HDIs, reset/boot-source separation, guest HDD writes, export/reimport, dirty-data warnings and both built-in floppy demos. Existing ordinary guest boot and memory-manager-off checks must remain meaningful.
- [ ] Add a targeted original guest memory-size diagnostic/test and production-release-Wasm Chromium validation on both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, including actual startup, driver initialization, largest DOS allocation, cold/reset, and restored default HDD; keep CI inputs legally distributable and lightweight. Don't multiply expensive full 128 MiB export tests where not needed.
- [ ] Run the repository's documented pinned fixture prep and license checks, native Rust tests, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, release Wasm build, strict nineteen-plus-intentional-assets publication audit and full two-root Chromium suite. Follow [test/CI performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles), report actual tests, times, failures, and any intentionally unchanged historical test hashes.
- [ ] Use English PR/review/commit communication and original Rust and guest test code; no game-specific patches, proprietary ROM/emulator code, adult-content HDIs, commercial assets, or human/gameplay/published-site checks required before merge.

## Optional validation

In a lawfully held private workspace, try the user-reported DOS game that needs approximately **540 KiB conventional memory**, with its installed HDD, and report only noncopyrighted memory/result metadata. This is not a mandatory CI/pre-merge gate; no game data may be uploaded. If useful and legally available, include a compatible PC-98 `MEM` utility in the boot image so users can inspect available memory themselves.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Deployment-only failures belong in separate `task` Issues, not in pre-merge acceptance.
